disagreements: Empirical depth error / SNR scale: pipeline box_noise = 85 ppm (snr_emp 10.0); my random-phase-box std = 45 ppm (SNR 20.0). My two cross-checks: single-box noise on the unfolded light curve / sqrt(24) = 42 ppm; per-event depth scatter / sqrt(24) = 72 ppm (inflated by one outlier event). The depth itself agrees (897+-45 vs 846+-52 formal); the pipeline's error is the more conservative and I cannot tell which detrend/noise definition is 'right' without reading its code.

Odd/even: same sense and size (odd shallower: 815+-68 vs 993+-59 ppm; pipeline 790 vs 911) but 1.99 sigma under my errors vs 0.71 sigma under the pipeline's. Dropping the single Q13-edge outlier event (epoch 28, an even epoch) gives 852+-59 vs 815+-67 ppm, 0.41 sigma.

Depth consistency in time: per-calendar-year depths 2009-2013 = 944+-170, 759+-107, 691+-72, 1067+-82, 880+-156 ppm, chi2 = 13.0 for 4 dof about the weighted mean (p~0.01); 2011 vs 2012 differ by 3.4 sigma. The pipeline's event-quartile depths show the same drift (713, 642, 807, 992). The drift is driven by epoch 28 (BKJD 1183.14, 0.40 d after the Q12/Q13 gap, in the noisiest quarter, local depth 2268+-349 ppm, 4.2-sigma pull); without it 2012 = 896+-81 ppm, per-year chi2 = 4.5/4, events chi2 = 19.1/22, global depth 831+-44 ppm. vet.json does not flag this event (its gap_frac_1d = 0.115 counts it only as 'near a gap').

# kic-006448637 — independent re-derivation (2026-10-17)

Candidate language only: this is a transit-like **signal** in the KBONUS-BKG light curve of KIC 6448637 (Gaia DR3 2077617724235317504, K dwarf, G = 15.73, Teff 5024 K, R* ~ 0.77 Rsun, 1006 pc, originating TPF KIC 6448574). Nothing here is a planet.

## What I did (no code from `pipeline/`, no wotan/TLS)
- Own loader: `LIGHTCURVE_STITCHED`, `SAP_QUALITY == 0` (33,566 of 45,938 cadences; 12 quarters Q2, Q4, Q5, Q8, Q10-17; baseline 1420.9 d), per-quarter median normalisation, SHA-256 of the FITS recorded in `results.json`.
- Own detrend: per-quarter time-windowed **1.0-d running median**, 2 iterations, points > 4 sigma above the trend excluded from the trend estimate (dips never excluded); search-stage clip +4/-6 sigma. Per-quarter robust scatter 465-530 ppm, except Q13 (874) and Q17 (868); used as the BLS weights.
- Own blind BLS 1-50 d: astropy `BoxLeastSquares`, log-uniform grid dlnP = 0.05/(3 x baseline) -> **333,518 trial periods x 8 durations (1.2-10 h)**, likelihood objective. Identical search on the inverted flux.
- Depth machinery of my own: out-of-transit mean minus in-box mean on a **re-detrend with |phase| < duration masked**; empirical error = std of ~3,900 same-duration boxes at random phases avoiding phases 0 and 0.5. Odd/even, secondary at phase 0.5, per-calendar-year depths, per-event local depths (+-1.5 d baseline, gap distance), box-SNR duration scan, trapezoid fit, and (as a cross-check only) an event-timing linear ephemeris.

## Results (PSF `FLUX`)
- **Blind BLS top-3 peaks: 35.58721 d (power 143.3), 17.79401 d (= P/2, 80.8), 11.86236 d (= P/3, 59.1).** The pipeline period is the top peak, blind, with its two sub-harmonics as the next peaks. Raw-spectrum SDE = **50.6** (42.8 after dividing out the period-dependent envelope). Inverted-flux null on the same grid: SDE 9.9, top peak 47.98 d, 479 ppm, 2.4 h — no comparable inverted signal.
- Refined ephemeris: **P = 35.58770 d**, t0 = 186.6804 BKJD = **BJD 2455019.6804** (epoch 0; mid-baseline epoch 19 is BJD 2455695.8468). Timing fit to 24 events: P = 35.58777 +- 0.00045 d (errors inflated x2.96 for chi2 193/22; rms timing residual 44 min, expected for SNR ~3-4 events).
- Duration: 4.13 h (BLS box), 4.32 h (box-SNR scan), **4.84 h trapezoid T14**, T23/T14 = 0.70 (flat-bottomed, not V-shaped; trapezoid and box fits give equal chi2). 
- **Depth 897 +- 45 ppm (empirical SNR 20.0, 174 in-transit cadences)** on the masked re-detrend; 723 ppm on the unmasked 1-d running-median detrend (the median window eats ~20% — same effect as the pipeline's pass-1 676 ppm vs pass-2 846 ppm). Trapezoid depth 886 ppm. Null-box mean 0.3 ppm; MAD-based error 46 ppm; white-noise expectation 44 ppm.
- Odd 815 +- 68 vs even 993 +- 59 ppm -> **1.99 sigma**; 0.41 sigma without the epoch-28 outlier (see below).
- Secondary at phase 0.5: **44 +- 44 ppm (0.98 sigma)**; deepest box anywhere in phase 0.2-0.8: 101 ppm at phase 0.63. No secondary.
- Transits: 40 epochs in the baseline, **26 with any in-transit cadence, 24 with >= 50% coverage** (expected 8.4 cadences per transit). All 24 local depths are positive; weighted mean 840 ppm; chi2 about the mean 36.0/23. Strongest single event carries 10% of the total SNR^2 — no single-event dominance.
- Per-year depths (2009-2013): **944 +- 170, 759 +- 107, 691 +- 72, 1067 +- 82, 880 +- 156 ppm**. chi2 = 13.0 for 4 dof about the weighted mean; 2011 vs 2012 differ by 3.4 sigma.

## SAP vs PSF (dilution check)
SAP_FLUX, same ephemeris and 4.13-h box on its own masked running-median detrend: **865 +- 49 ppm** (SNR 17.6; odd 820, even 918, secondary 2 ppm). **SAP/PSF depth ratio = 0.96 +- 0.07.** The catalogue crowdsap = 0.94 predicts a ratio ~0.94-0.99 if the eclipsing source is the target star itself (SAP is diluted by ~6% neighbour light; PSF is not). The observed ratio is consistent with that and with 1.0: the PSF de-blending neither manufactures nor substantially suppresses the signal, and SAP shows no extra depth that a bright neighbour fully inside the aperture but outside the PSF model would add. It does **not** exclude a contaminating eclipsing binary that the PSF fit partly absorbs (G = 16.03 Gaia neighbour at ~2.6 px / ~10 arcsec; psffrac is only 0.50); that is what the pixel-level test is for, and this ratio cannot substitute for it.

## Comparison with the pipeline (`vet.json`, read only after the above)
Agrees: period (1.0 sigma), t0 (8 min), depth (897 +- 45 vs 846 +- 52 formal; the pipeline's wider 4.5-h box is expected to be shallower), duration (4.1-4.8 h vs fixed 4.5 h), odd/even sense and size, no secondary, 26 events, events chi2 (36/23 vs 35/25), the depth drift across the baseline (my years vs its quartiles). **Recovered blind: yes.**

Honest disagreements (details in `comparison.json`):
1. **Error scale.** My random-phase-box error (45 ppm; single-box-noise/sqrt(N) 42 ppm) is half the pipeline's box_noise (85 ppm), so my empirical SNR is 20 vs its 10. Per-event scatter/sqrt(N) gives 72 ppm, between the two, and is inflated by one event. Either way the signal is well above 10 sigma; the pipeline's figure is the conservative one and should be the quoted one.
2. **Depth consistency in time is only marginal with all data** (per-year chi2 13/4, p ~ 0.01; odd/even 2.0 sigma). Both tensions trace to **epoch 28 (BKJD 1183.14, Q13 start, 0.40 d after the Q12/Q13 gap, local depth 2268 +- 349 ppm, 4.2-sigma pull in the noisiest quarter)**. Excluding it: global depth 831 +- 44 ppm, 2012 = 896 +- 81, per-year chi2 4.5/4, events chi2 19/22, odd/even 0.4 sigma. The pipeline keeps this event; a human should look at it on `fold_events.png` and at the Q13 start before anything is quoted. I did not drop it from the headline numbers (that would be a post-hoc choice).

## Context noted after the fact
`pixel.json` (read only after my numbers) reports that in 0 of 13 usable quarters the event-differenced deficit is closer to the target than to any other Gaia source (median target-to-deficit 95 arcsec, median peak SNR 3.6, median in-aperture depth 87 ppm on the KIC 6448574 TPF). That is outside this re-derivation, but it means the light-curve agreement above says nothing about *which* star eclipses; the signal stays a signal, not a candidate, until localisation is resolved.

## Files
All under `/home/user/ZyushgPlanet/runs/poolA_main/adversarial/kic-006448637/rederive/`: `rederive_kic006448637.py` (search + statistics + figure), `compare_with_pipeline.py` (extra noise estimates, outlier test, timing fit, comparison), `results.json`, `comparison.json`, `events.csv`, `fold.png`, `bls_periodogram.npz`, `run.log`.
sap_vs_psf_depth: SAP_FLUX depth 865 +- 49 ppm vs PSF FLUX depth 897 +- 45 ppm at the same ephemeris and 4.13-h box (each on its own masked 1-d running-median detrend): ratio SAP/PSF = 0.96 +- 0.07. With crowdsap = 0.94 (median SAP/PSF flux level 0.86 = flfrcsap) an on-target eclipse predicts a ratio of ~0.94-0.99, so the observed ratio is consistent with the signal being carried by the target's PSF flux with no extra dilution or enhancement in the aperture sum; i.e. the PSF de-blending neither creates nor suppresses the signal. It does not by itself exclude a neighbouring eclipsing source that the PSF fit partly absorbs (psffrac = 0.50; G = 16.0 Gaia neighbour ~10 arcsec away) -- that question belongs to the pixel-level test, which per pixel.json is unresolved for this star.
